title.zh: 卷117 志九十二 职官四
title.raw: 卷117 志九十二 职官四

translations.literal: Treatise ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 92

translations.literal: Offices, part four.
translations.idiomatic: Offices IV

translations.literal: Military offices, frontier-department offices, and native-chieftain offices.
translations.idiomatic: Military Offices, Frontier Departments, and Native Chieftain Officials

sentences.zh: 公侯伯子男額駙侍衛處鑾輿衛

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, imperial sons-in-law, the Imperial Bodyguard Office, and the Imperial Carriage Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Ranks, Imperial Sons-in-Law, the Imperial Bodyguard Office, and the Imperial Carriage Guard

sentences.zh: 驍騎營八旗都統前鋒營護軍營統領

translations.literal: Vanguard Cavalry Brigade, Eight Banners commanders-in-chief, vanguard brigade, guard brigade, and their commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Cavalry Brigade, Eight Banners Commanders-in-Chief, Vanguard and Guard Brigades, and Their Commanders

sentences.zh: 景運門直班圓明園八旗內務府三旗護軍營總統三旗包衣驍騎營三旗包衣護軍營

translations.literal: Straight duty at the Jingyun Gate, Eight Banners of the Yuanmingyuan, Internal Affairs Office Three-Banner guard brigade commander-in-chief, Three-Banner bond-servant vanguard cavalry brigade, and Three-Banner bond-servant guard brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyun Gate Direct Duty, Yuanmingyuan Eight Banners, Internal Affairs Three-Banner Guard and Bond-Servant Vanguard and Guard Brigades

sentences.zh: 步軍統領火器健銳神機虎槍諸營嚮導處上虞備用處善撲營王公府屬各官

translations.literal: Foot-soldier commander-in-chief, fire-arms, select crack troops, divine engine, tiger gun, and other brigades, guide office, Shangyu reserve office, wrestling brigade, and officials attached to princely mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Foot Brigade Commander-in-Chief, Firearms and Elite Brigades, Guide and Reserve Offices, Wrestling Brigade, and Princely Household Officials

sentences.zh: 公主府長史陵寢駐防各官各省駐防將軍等官提督等官各處駐劄大臣

translations.literal: Princess-mansion chamberlains, tomb-garrison officials, provincial garrison generals and the like, provincial military governors and the like, and resident ministers posted at various places.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Household Chamberlains, Tomb Garrisons, Provincial Garrison Generals, Provincial Military Governors, and Resident Ministers

sentences.zh: 回部各官籓屬各官土司各官番部僧官

translations.literal: Officials of the Muslim regions, dependent-territory officials, native-chieftain officials, and clerical officials of the frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Muslim Region Officials, Dependent-Territory Officials, Native Chieftains, and Frontier Clerical Officials

translations.literal: Duke, marquis, and earl — above the regular ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Duke, marquis, and earl — ranks above the regular scale.

translations.literal: Viscount — regular first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Viscount — regular first rank.

translations.literal: Baron — regular second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Baron — regular second rank.

translations.literal: Commandant of Light Chariots — regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Light Chariots — regular third rank.

translations.literal: All of the above are divided into three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the above was divided into three grades.

translations.literal: Commandant of Cavalry — regular fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cavalry — regular fourth rank.

translations.literal: Commandant of Cloud Cavalry — regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cloud Cavalry — regular fifth rank.

translations.literal: Commandant of Grace Cavalry — regular seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Grace Cavalry — regular seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 凡九等，以封功臣及外戚。

translations.literal: In all nine grades, used to ennoble meritorious ministers and maternal relatives.
translations.idiomatic: There were nine grades in all, conferred to reward meritorious ministers and imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 初，天命五年，論功序列五爵，分總兵為三等，副將、參將、游擊亦如之，牛錄額真稱備御。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the fifth year of Tianming, merit was assessed and five noble ranks were ordered; commanders-in-chief were divided into three grades, as were deputy commanders, assistant commanders, and mobile detach commanders; niru ejen were called beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, in the fifth year of Tianming (1620), merit was assessed and five noble ranks were established; commanders-in-chief were divided into three grades, as were deputy commanders, assistant commanders, and mobile-detach commanders, and niru ejen were styled beiyu.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，始設一等公，即五備御之總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong, a first-grade duke was first established — that is, the commander-in-chief among the five beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiancong (1634), the first-grade duke was instituted — the commander-in-chief among the five beiyu.

sentences.zh: 及一、二、三等昂邦章京，即總兵。

translations.literal: And first-, second-, and third-grade angbang janggin — that is, commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: First-, second-, and third-grade angbang janggin corresponded to commanders-in-chief.

translations.literal: Mele janggin — that is, deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Mele janggin corresponded to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 扎蘭章京，一、二等即參將，三等游擊。

translations.literal: Jalan janggin: first and second grades were assistant commanders; third grade, mobile-detach commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jalan janggin: the first and second grades were assistant commanders; the third grade, mobile-detach commander.

translations.literal: Niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Niru janggin

translations.literal: That is, beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Corresponded to beiyu.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，加封功臣公、侯、伯世爵，錫之誥券。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, meritorious ministers were further ennobled with hereditary ranks of duke, marquis, and earl, and granted patent letters of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi (1644), meritorious ministers received additional hereditary ranks of duke, marquis, and earl, together with patent letters of investiture.

sentences.zh: 時公、侯、伯下無子、男，副、參即其爵也。

translations.literal: At that time, below duke, marquis, and earl there were no viscount or baron ranks; deputy and assistant commanders held those noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were no viscount or baron ranks below duke, marquis, and earl; deputy and assistant commanders held the corresponding noble titles.

sentences.zh: 四年，改昂邦章京為精奇尼哈番，梅勒章京為阿思哈尼哈番，扎蘭章京為阿達哈哈番，牛錄章京為拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, angbang janggin was changed to jingqini hafan, mele janggin to ashani hafan, jalan janggin to adaha hafan, and niru janggin to baitalabule hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1647), angbang janggin became jingqini hafan, mele janggin ashani hafan, jalan janggin adaha hafan, and niru janggin baitalabule hafan.

sentences.zh: 授爵自拖沙喇哈番始，舊為半個前程，漢稱外所千總，正五品。

translations.literal: Ennoblement began with tasahala hafan, formerly half a qian-cheng; in Chinese called battalion commander of an outer post, regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Noble rank began with tasahala hafan, formerly half a qian-cheng; in Chinese usage this was the battalion commander of an outer post, regular fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 遞上為拜他喇布勒哈番，漢稱外衛指揮副僉事，從四品。

translations.literal: Ascending one step was baitalabule hafan; in Chinese called assistant commissioner of an outer guard, subordinate fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One step higher was baitalabule hafan, called in Chinese the assistant commissioner of an outer guard, subordinate fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 再一拖沙喇哈番，稱外衛指揮僉事，正四品。

translations.literal: With one more tasahala hafan, it was called commissioner of an outer guard, regular fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: With another tasahala hafan added, the title was commissioner of an outer guard, regular fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 阿達哈哈番，三等稱外衛副同知，二等稱外衛指揮同知，俱從三品。

translations.literal: Adaha hafan: third grade was called deputy intendant of an outer guard, second grade assistant commander of an outer guard — both subordinate third rank.
translations.idiomatic: For adaha hafan, the third grade was deputy intendant of an outer guard and the second grade assistant commander of an outer guard — both subordinate third rank.

sentences.zh: 一等稱外衛指揮副使，再一拖沙喇哈番，稱外衛指揮使，正三品。

translations.literal: First grade was called vice commander of an outer guard; with one more tasahala hafan, commander of an outer guard, regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The first grade was vice commander of an outer guard; with another tasahala hafan added, commander of an outer guard, regular third rank.

sentences.zh: 阿思哈尼哈番，三等稱外衛都指揮副同知，二等稱外衛都指揮同知，俱從二品。

translations.literal: Ashani hafan: third grade was called deputy intendant of the chief command of an outer guard, second grade assistant chief commander of an outer guard — both subordinate second rank.
translations.idiomatic: For ashani hafan, the third grade was deputy intendant of the chief command of an outer guard and the second grade assistant chief commander of an outer guard — both subordinate second rank.

sentences.zh: 一等稱外衛都指揮副使，再一拖沙喇哈番，稱外衛都指揮使，俱正二品。

translations.literal: First grade was called vice chief commander of an outer guard; with one more tasahala hafan, chief commander of an outer guard — both regular second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The first grade was vice chief commander of an outer guard; with another tasahala hafan added, chief commander of an outer guard — both regular second rank.

translations.literal: Jingqini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqini hafan

sentences.zh: 二等稱鑾儀衛都指揮同知，從一品。

translations.literal: Second grade was called assistant chief commander of the Imperial Carriage Guard, subordinate first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The second grade was assistant chief commander of the Imperial Carriage Guard, subordinate first rank.

sentences.zh: 一等稱鑾儀衛都指揮使，正一品。

translations.literal: First grade was called chief commander of the Imperial Carriage Guard, regular first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The first grade was chief commander of the Imperial Carriage Guard, regular first rank.

sentences.zh: 積拖沙喇哈番二十六，為一等公。

translations.literal: Accumulating twenty-six tasahala hafan made a first-grade duke.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six accumulated tasahala hafan constituted a first-grade duke.

translations.literal: In the eighth year, perpetual hereditary succession was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1651), perpetual hereditary succession was established.

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, consolidated inheritance was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1661), consolidated inheritance was established.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，以世爵合併至公、侯、伯者，仍與分襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, where hereditary noble ranks had been consolidated up to duke, marquis, or earl, separate inheritance was still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi (1662), where hereditary ranks had been consolidated up to duke, marquis, or earl, separate inheritance was still allowed.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，錫明裔硃之璉一等候。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, the Ming descendant Zhu Zhilian was granted a first-grade marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng (1724), the Ming descendant Zhu Zhilian received a first-grade marquisate.

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, the name Yan'en was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong (1749), the title Yan'en was conferred.

sentences.zh: 八年，嘉大學士張廷玉等輔弼勤勞，賜一等阿達哈哈番世襲，漢世職自此始。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu and others were praised for diligent service as counselors; a first-grade adaha hafan with hereditary succession was granted — hereditary Chinese offices began from this.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1743), Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu and others were rewarded for diligent counsel with a hereditary first-grade adaha hafan — hereditary offices for Chinese officials began here.

translations.literal: The next year, honorable ducal names were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, honorific ducal names were conferred.

translations.literal: Such as Baoji and Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: Examples include Baoji and Zhongda.

translations.literal: Maternal relatives were ordered to be styled Duke Who Receives Grace.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial affines were styled Duke Who Receives Grace.

translations.literal: Formerly the regulation was first-grade duke.
translations.idiomatic: Under the earlier regulation this was a first-grade duke.

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong it was changed to third grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of Qianlong (1778) it was reduced to third grade.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，定精奇尼哈番漢字為子，阿思哈尼哈番為男，阿達哈哈番為輕車都尉，拜他喇布勒哈番為騎都尉，拖沙喇哈番為雲騎尉，滿文如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, jingqini hafan was fixed in Chinese characters as zi (viscount), ashani hafan as nan (baron), adaha hafan as Commandant of Light Chariots, baitalabule hafan as Commandant of Cavalry, and tasahala hafan as Commandant of Cloud Cavalry; Manchu remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong (1736), jingqini hafan was rendered in Chinese as viscount, ashani hafan as baron, adaha hafan as Commandant of Light Chariots, baitalabule hafan as Commandant of Cavalry, and tasahala hafan as Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, while the Manchu forms were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定公、侯、伯以次封爵表。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the table of ennoblement descending from duke, marquis, and earl was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1748), the descending table of ennoblement from duke, marquis, and earl was fixed.

sentences.zh: 一等公襲二十六次，一等候兼一雲騎尉襲二十三次，一等伯兼一雲騎尉十九次，一等男兼一雲騎尉十一次，自公至男，一、二、三等依次遞降。

translations.literal: A first-grade duke was inherited twenty-six times; a first-grade marquis with one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, twenty-three times; a first-grade earl with one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, nineteen times; a first-grade baron with one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, eleven times; from duke to baron, first, second, and third grades descended in order.
translations.idiomatic: A first-grade duke passed twenty-six inheritances; a first-grade marquis with one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, twenty-three; a first-grade earl with one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, nineteen; a first-grade baron with one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, eleven; from duke to baron, the first, second, and third grades descended in sequence.

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, honorable names for marquis and earl were retroactively bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1749), honorific names for marquisates and earldoms were conferred retroactively.

translations.literal: Such as Marquis Who Upholds Righteousness and Earl Who Shows Kind Favor.
translations.idiomatic: Examples include Marquis Who Upholds Righteousness and Earl Who Shows Kind Favor.

translations.literal: From this it was handed down as perpetual regulation.
translations.idiomatic: From then on this became the permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 十六年，定世襲七品官為恩騎尉，是為九等。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the hereditary seventh-rank office was fixed as Commandant of Grace Cavalry — this was the ninth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1751), the hereditary seventh-rank office was fixed as Commandant of Grace Cavalry — the ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，嘉黃芳度功，予襲公爵十二世，並依八旗例，復給恩騎尉，優恤於無窮。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, Huang Fangdu's merit was praised; he was granted ducal inheritance for twelve generations, and according to the Eight Banners precedent a Commandant of Grace Cavalry was again given — favor extending without limit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year (1767), Huang Fangdu was rewarded for merit with twelve generations of ducal inheritance and, following Eight Banners precedent, an additional Commandant of Grace Cavalry — favor without end.

sentences.zh: 時將軍張勇等，提督孫思克等，並緣此推恩，繇是漢官亦有世襲罔替例。

translations.literal: At that time Generals Zhang Yong and others and provincial military governors Sun Sike and others likewise received extended grace; henceforth Chinese officials also had the precedent of perpetual hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Generals such as Zhang Yong and provincial military governors such as Sun Sike received the same extended favor, and from then on Chinese officials too had cases of perpetual hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 同治中興，剖符析圭者，漢官為多，猶古武功爵也。

translations.literal: In the Tongzhi restoration, those who received investiture tablets and jade scepters were mostly Chinese officials — still the ancient military-merit nobility.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi restoration, most of those who received noble investiture were Chinese officials — much like the ancient nobility of military merit.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十三年，制定創興大業者予子、男，號曰商爵，則頒爵之制少異已。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu, it was fixed that founders of great enterprises should receive viscount or baron — styled merchant nobility — and the system of conferring noble rank differed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu (1907), founders of great enterprises were granted viscount or baron ranks styled merchant nobility, and the system of ennoblement changed somewhat.

translations.literal: Imperial sons-in-law of princesses — rank above marquis and earl.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law of princesses ranked above marquises and earls.

sentences.zh: 尚固倫公主中宮所生女。

translations.literal: When marrying a Gulun princess — a daughter born to the empress in the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: For marriage to a Gulun princess, a daughter born to the empress:

sentences.zh: 曰固倫額駙，秩視固山貝子；

translations.literal: He was called Gulun efu; his rank was equal to a gushan beise;
translations.idiomatic: The title was Gulun efu, with rank equal to a gushan beise;

sentences.zh: 尚和碩公主妃所生女及中宮撫養者。

translations.literal: When marrying a Heshuo princess — a daughter born to a consort or one raised by the empress.
translations.idiomatic: For marriage to a Heshuo princess, a daughter born to a consort or raised by the empress:

sentences.zh: 曰和碩額駙，秩視超品公。

translations.literal: He was called Heshuo efu; his rank was equal to a duke above the regular scale.
translations.idiomatic: The title was Heshuo efu, with rank equal to a duke above the regular scale.

sentences.zh: 親王女曰郡主，額駙秩視武職一品。

translations.literal: A prince's daughter was called junzhu; the efu's rank was equal to first-grade military rank.
translations.idiomatic: A prince's daughter was styled junzhu; her son-in-law's rank equaled first-grade military rank.

sentences.zh: 世子、郡王女曰縣主，額駙視二品。

translations.literal: An heir apparent's or prince of the second degree's daughter was called xianzhu; the efu was treated as second rank.
translations.idiomatic: An heir apparent's or commandery prince's daughter was styled xianzhu; her son-in-law ranked as second grade.

sentences.zh: 貝勒女曰郡君，額駙視三品。

translations.literal: A beile's daughter was called junjun; the efu was treated as third rank.
translations.idiomatic: A beile's daughter was styled junjun; her son-in-law ranked as third grade.

sentences.zh: 貝子女曰縣君，額駙視四品。

translations.literal: A bei's daughter was called xianjun; the efu was treated as fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: A bei's daughter was styled xianjun; her son-in-law ranked as fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 入八分鎮國公、輔國公女曰鄉君，額駙視五品。

translations.literal: Daughters of the Eight-Point Duke Who Guards the State and Duke Who Assists the State were called xiangjun; the efu was treated as fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters of dukes who had entered the eight points were styled xiangjun; their sons-in-law ranked as fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 近支格格予歲祿，遠支止予虛銜。

translations.literal: Gege of the close lineage received annual stipends; those of the distant lineage received only nominal titles.
translations.idiomatic: Gege of the close lineage received annual stipends; those of the distant lineage received only nominal titles.

translations.literal: When marrying down into Mongol dependencies, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied when they married into Mongol dependencies.

sentences.zh: 所生之子，各予其父品級。

translations.literal: Sons born to them were each granted their father's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sons born to them received their father's rank.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖時，額駙何和禮授都統，達爾漢繼之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the time of Taizu, the efu Heheli was appointed commander-in-chief; Darhan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, under Taizu, the son-in-law Heheli was appointed commander-in-chief, succeeded by Darhan.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，巴雅思祜朗授都統，拉哈繼之。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizong, Bayasihulang was appointed commander-in-chief; Laha succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, Bayasihulang was appointed commander-in-chief, succeeded by Laha.

sentences.zh: 自是御前侍衛大臣、護軍前鋒統領，皆為專職。

translations.literal: From this, grand ministers of the imperial bodyguard before the throne and commanders of the guard and vanguard became specialized posts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter grand ministers of the imperial bodyguard and commanders of the guard and vanguard became specialized posts.

sentences.zh: 亦有僅受歲祿，而護從隨征受命一充其任者。

translations.literal: There were also some who received only annual stipends but, attending and following on campaign, accepted orders to fill such posts once.
translations.idiomatic: Some received only stipends but on campaign were ordered once to fill such posts while attending the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至出鎮西北，則自定邊左副將軍策凌始。

translations.literal: As for commanding the northwest, this began with Celing as Left Deputy General Who Settles the Frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Command of the northwest began with Celing as Left Deputy General Who Settles the Frontier.

sentences.zh: 踵其後者，世宗時，觀音保為領隊大臣，高宗時，色布騰巴勒珠爾為參贊大臣。

translations.literal: Those who followed: under Shizong, Guanyinbao as column-leading minister; under Gaozong, Sebuteng Balzhu'er as assisting minister.
translations.idiomatic: Later examples include Guanyinbao as column-leading minister under the Yongzheng Emperor and Sebuteng Balzhu'er as assisting minister under the Qianlong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 其授文職者，止天命間蘇鼐、乾隆間福隆安二尚書而已。

translations.literal: Those appointed to civil offices were only Su Tai in the Tianming period and Fu Long'an in the Qianlong period — two ministers alone.
translations.idiomatic: Only two received civil appointments: Su Tai in the Tianming period and Fu Long'an in the Qianlong period — both as ministers.

sentences.zh: 侍衛處領侍衛內大臣，正一品。

translations.literal: The Imperial Bodyguard Office: leading grand minister of the imperial bodyguard — regular first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Bodyguard Office: leading grand minister of the imperial bodyguard — regular first rank.

sentences.zh: 內大臣，初制正一品，後改從一品。

translations.literal: Grand ministers of the imperial bodyguard: originally regular first rank, later changed to subordinate first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers of the imperial bodyguard: originally regular first rank, later changed to subordinate first rank.

translations.literal: Six each.
translations.idiomatic: Six in each category.

sentences.zh: 鑲黃、正黃、正白旗各二人。

translations.literal: Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White Banners — two each.
translations.idiomatic: Two each for the Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White Banners.

sentences.zh: 散秩大臣、都統、護軍前鋒統領、滿大學士、尚書內特簡。

translations.literal: Ministers without portfolio, commanders-in-chief, commanders of guard and vanguard, Manchu grand secretaries, and ministers were specially selected from among them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers without portfolio, banner commanders-in-chief, guard and vanguard commanders, Manchu grand secretaries, and ministers were specially selected for these posts.

translations.literal: Ministers without portfolio had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There was no fixed quota for ministers without portfolio.

translations.literal: Subordinate second rank, receiving third-rank salary.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate second rank, with third-rank salary.

translations.literal: One director.
translations.idiomatic: One director.

translations.literal: Three acting directors.
translations.idiomatic: Three acting directors.

translations.literal: Twenty-seven clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven clerks.

translations.literal: Fifteen internal acting appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen internal acting appointees.

sentences.zh: 協理事務侍衛班領，正三品。

translations.literal: Squad leader of bodyguards assisting in affairs — regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Squad leader of bodyguards assisting in affairs — regular third rank.

translations.literal: Squad leader of bodyguards — regular fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Squad leader of bodyguards — regular fourth rank.

translations.literal: Twelve each.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve in each category.

translations.literal: Twenty-four acting squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four acting squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 侍衛什長七十有九人，宗室九人。

translations.literal: Seventy-nine corporals of bodyguards, nine of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-nine bodyguard corporals, nine from the imperial clan.

translations.literal: First-grade bodyguards — regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: First-grade bodyguards — regular third rank.

translations.literal: Sixty men — twenty from each banner.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty men — twenty from each banner.

translations.literal: Nine from the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Nine from the imperial clan.

translations.literal: Three from each banner.
translations.idiomatic: Three from each banner.

translations.literal: Second grade — regular fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Second grade — regular fourth rank.

translations.literal: One hundred fifty men — fifty from each banner.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred fifty men — fifty from each banner.

translations.literal: Third grade — regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Third grade — regular fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 二百七十人，旗各九十人。

translations.literal: Two hundred seventy men — ninety from each banner.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred seventy men — ninety from each banner.

translations.literal: Sixty-three from the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-three from the imperial clan.

translations.literal: Twenty-one from each banner.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one from each banner.

translations.literal: Ninety blue-plume bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety blue-plume bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 旗各三十人，三旗通為五百七十人。

translations.literal: Thirty from each banner — five hundred seventy in all for the three banners.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty from each banner, five hundred seventy in all across the three banners.

sentences.zh: 內隸黏竿處三十四人，上駟院二十四人，上虞備用處三十六人。

translations.literal: Thirty-four attached to the Sticky-Pole Office, twenty-four to the Imperial Stud, thirty-six to the Upper Honorary Reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-four attached to the Sticky-Pole Office, twenty-four to the Imperial Stud, and thirty-six to the Upper Honorary Reserve.

translations.literal: The Wrestling Battalion and the Armory had no fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The Wrestling Battalion and the Armory had no fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 四等侍衛、漢侍衛，分一、二、三等及藍翎。

translations.literal: Fourth-grade bodyguards and Han bodyguards were divided into first, second, and third grades and blue plume.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-grade and Han bodyguards were divided into first, second, and third grades, plus blue plume.

translations.literal: All without fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: None had fixed quotas.

translations.literal: Personal-guard corporals — regular sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Personal-guard corporals — regular sixth rank.

translations.literal: Acting personal-guard corporals — initially without rank.
translations.idiomatic: Acting personal-guard corporals initially had no rank.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年定從八品。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong, fixed at subordinate eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 51 they were fixed at subordinate eighth rank.

translations.literal: Seventy-seven each.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-seven in each category.

sentences.zh: 領侍衛掌董帥侍衛親軍，偕內大臣、散秩大臣翊衛扈從。

translations.literal: The leading bodyguard minister supervised and commanded bodyguards and the personal guard, and together with grand ministers of the bodyguard and ministers without portfolio assisted in protection and escort.
translations.idiomatic: The leading bodyguard minister directed bodyguards and the personal guard, and together with grand ministers of the bodyguard and ministers without portfolio provided close protection and escort.

sentences.zh: 協理、主事、筆帖式，分掌章奏文移。

translations.literal: Coordinators, directors, and clerks separately managed memorials and documents.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinators, directors, and clerks handled memorials and paperwork respectively.

sentences.zh: 侍衛掌營衛周廬，更番侍直。

translations.literal: Bodyguards managed camp defense and the palace perimeter, rotating watch duty.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguards managed camp security and the palace perimeter on rotating watch.

translations.literal: They were divided into two wings for palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: They were divided into two wings for palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 乾清門、內右門、神武門、寧壽門為內班，太和門為外班。

translations.literal: Qianqing Gate, Inner Right Gate, Divine Martial Gate, and Ningshou Gate formed the inner shift; Taihe Gate the outer shift.
translations.idiomatic: The inner shift covered Qianqing Gate, Inner Right Gate, Divine Martial Gate, and Ningshou Gate; Taihe Gate was the outer shift.

translations.literal: On imperial tours, encampments followed palace regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours, encampments followed the same regulations as within the palace.

sentences.zh: 朝會、祭祀出入，則衛官填街，騎士塞路。

translations.literal: At court assemblies and when entering or leaving for sacrifices, guard officers filled the streets and horsemen blocked the roads.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies and sacrificial processions, guard officers lined the streets and cavalry blocked the roads.

sentences.zh: 領侍衛內大臣、侍衛班領，帥豹尾班侍衛。

translations.literal: Leading bodyguard grand ministers and bodyguard squad leaders commanded the leopard-tail guard bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: Leading bodyguard grand ministers and squad leaders commanded the leopard-tail guard bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 散秩大臣、侍衛什長，執纛親軍以供導從，大閱則按隊環衛。

translations.literal: Ministers without portfolio and bodyguard corporals bore banners with the personal guard for escort; at grand reviews they encircled in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers without portfolio and bodyguard corporals carried standards with the personal guard for escort; at grand reviews they formed encircling ranks.

translations.literal: Personal-guard corporals commanded subdivisions of the camp force.
translations.idiomatic: Personal-guard corporals commanded subdivisions of the camp troops.

sentences.zh: 其常日侍直者，御前大臣、王大臣兼任。

translations.literal: Those on daily watch duty were concurrently served by imperial-front ministers and princely ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Daily watch duty was concurrently held by imperial-front ministers and princely ministers.

sentences.zh: 御前侍衛、御前行走、乾清門行走，俱侍衛內特簡。

translations.literal: Imperial-front bodyguards, imperial-front attendants, and Qianqing Gate attendants were all specially selected from among bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial-front bodyguards, imperial-front attendants, and Qianqing Gate attendants were all specially chosen from the bodyguard corps.

translations.literal: No fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There was no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 故事，凡宿衛之臣，惟滿員授乾清門侍衛，其重以貴戚或異材，乃擢入御前。

translations.literal: By precedent, of all palace-guard officials, only Manchus were appointed Qianqing Gate bodyguards; only when weight was given to noble kin or exceptional talent was one promoted to the imperial front.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, only Manchus among palace guards received Qianqing Gate appointments; promotion to the imperial front required noble birth or exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 漢籍輒除大門上侍衛，領侍衛內大臣轄之。

translations.literal: Han registry members were always appointed outer-gate bodyguards, under the leading bodyguard grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials were routinely appointed as outer-gate bodyguards under the leading bodyguard grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 其以材勇擢侍乾清門者，班崇極矣。

translations.literal: Those promoted for courage and ability to serve at Qianqing Gate had reached the highest honor of the corps.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion to Qianqing Gate service for courage and ability marked the highest honor in the corps.

sentences.zh: 惟嘉慶問楊芳特授國什哈轄，漢國什哈內大臣，歎為未有。

translations.literal: Only in the Jiaqing era was Yang Fang specially granted jurisdiction as Guoshiha and made a Han Guoshiha grand minister — acclaimed as unprecedented.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Jiaqing era was Yang Fang specially made Guoshiha commander and Han Guoshiha grand minister — hailed as unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 其出入扈從者，後扈大臣二人，御前大臣、領侍衛內大臣兼任。

translations.literal: Those who escorted on entry and exit: two rear-escort ministers, concurrently held by imperial-front ministers and leading bodyguard grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Escort on imperial movements included two rear-escort ministers, concurrently held by imperial-front and leading bodyguard grand ministers.

translations.literal: Ten forward-leading ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Ten forward-leading ministers.

sentences.zh: 內大臣、散秩大臣、前鋒統領、護軍統領、副都統兼任。

translations.literal: Concurrently held by grand ministers of the bodyguard, ministers without portfolio, vanguard commanders, guard commanders, and deputy commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: These posts were concurrently held by bodyguard grand ministers, ministers without portfolio, vanguard and guard commanders, and deputy commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 所轄奏事處，御前大臣兼管。

translations.literal: The Memorial Office under their jurisdiction was jointly managed by imperial-front ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial Office under their jurisdiction was jointly supervised by imperial-front ministers.

sentences.zh: 侍衛一人，御前侍衛、乾清門侍衛內特簡。

translations.literal: One bodyguard, specially selected from imperial-front and Qianqing Gate bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: One bodyguard, specially chosen from imperial-front and Qianqing Gate bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 章京六人，內府司員四人。

translations.literal: Six secretaries — four from the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Six secretaries, four from the Imperial Household Department.

translations.literal: Two from the boards and courts.
translations.idiomatic: Two from the boards and courts.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式二人，內府筆帖式兼充。

translations.literal: Two clerks, filled concurrently by Imperial Household clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Two clerks, concurrently filled from the Imperial Household.

translations.literal: Six bodyguards for presenting Mongol affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Six bodyguards for Mongol memorials.

sentences.zh: 乾清門或大門侍衛兼充。

translations.literal: Filled concurrently by Qianqing Gate or outer-gate bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: Filled concurrently by Qianqing Gate or outer-gate bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以八旗禁旅戡定區夏，鑲黃、正黃、正白三旗皆自將，爰遴其子弟，命曰侍衛，亦間及宗室秀彥、外籓侍子，統以勳戚，備環直焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning, the Taizu, with the Eight Banners' forbidden brigades, pacified the realm; the Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White Banners he all commanded in person, and then selected their sons and younger brothers, naming them bodyguards — also occasionally including outstanding imperial-clan youths and sons of outer vassals — placing them under meritorious kin, to stand guard in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning the Taizu, using the Eight Banners' elite forces, pacified the realm. He personally led the Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White Banners, chose their sons and younger kinsmen as bodyguards—sometimes also outstanding clansmen and sons of outer vassals—and placed them under meritorious relatives for rotating palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，定侍衛處員數。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the quotas of the Bodyguard Office were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 the Bodyguard Office quotas were fixed.

translations.literal: As listed above.
translations.idiomatic: As listed above.

translations.literal: At the time Han hereditary students were also selected, but this was soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Han hereditary students were also selected at first, but the practice was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，擢武進士嫻騎射者為侍衛，附三旗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi, military jinshi skilled in riding and archery were promoted as bodyguards, attached to the three banners.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 military jinshi skilled in riding and archery were promoted as bodyguards attached to the three banners.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，增宗室侍衛，無常員。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, imperial-clan bodyguards were increased — no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: In year 37 imperial-clan bodyguards were added without a fixed quota.

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng, fixed at ninety men.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 7 the quota was fixed at ninety.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，選藍翎侍衛材力魁健者置四等。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, robust blue-plume bodyguards were selected and placed in a fourth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 the sturdiest blue-plume bodyguards were selected for a fourth grade.

translations.literal: Later it was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later the arrangement was restored.

sentences.zh: 明年，定武進士一甲一名授一等侍衛，二、三名授二等，二甲選三等，三甲選藍翎，置滿洲主事一人。

translations.literal: The next year it was fixed: one first-place military jinshi received first-grade bodyguard; second and third places second grade; from the second class, third grade; from the third class, blue plume — and one Manchu director was established.
translations.idiomatic: The next year: the top military jinshi received first-grade bodyguard; second and third places second grade; second-class graduates third grade; third-class blue plume; and one Manchu director was added.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，以隨印協理事務侍衛班領為一等，侍衛班領為二等。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, the squad leader of bodyguards assisting in affairs with the seal was made first grade, and the bodyguard squad leader second grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 the seal-attending squad leader assisting in affairs became first grade and the ordinary squad leader second grade.

sentences.zh: 凡十人置一長，三旗什長六十人，宗室九人。

translations.literal: In general one leader was placed over every ten men; sixty corporals for the three banners, nine from the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Generally one leader oversaw every ten men; sixty banner corporals and nine from the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 四十年，增委署親軍校七十有七人。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, seventy-seven acting personal-guard corporals were added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 seventy-seven acting personal-guard corporals were added.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，以散秩大臣無辦事責，諭凡擢都統者停兼職。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing, because ministers without portfolio had no administrative duties, an edict ordered that all promoted to commander-in-chief cease holding concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19, since ministers without portfolio had no administrative duties, an edict required those promoted to commander-in-chief to give up concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 鑾輿衛掌衛事大臣一人。

translations.literal: The Imperial Carriage Guard: one minister supervising guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Carriage Guard: one minister supervising guard affairs.

translations.literal: Regular first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Regular first rank.

sentences.zh: 無專員，以滿、蒙王、公、大臣兼授。

translations.literal: No dedicated appointee — conferred concurrently on Manchu and Mongol princes, dukes, and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: There was no dedicated post; Manchu and Mongol princes, dukes, and ministers held it concurrently.

translations.literal: Imperial carriage commissioners — originally regular second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial carriage commissioners were originally regular second rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年改正三品，七年復故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi changed to regular third rank; in the seventh year restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 they were lowered to regular third rank; in year 7 the original rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 滿洲二人，凡滿缺並以蒙古人兼授。

translations.literal: Two Manchus — for all Manchu posts Mongols were also concurrently appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Two Manchus; for all Manchu posts Mongols were also appointed concurrently.

translations.literal: One Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: One Han Banner post.

sentences.zh: 凡漢軍缺並以漢人兼授。

translations.literal: For all Han Banner posts Han Chinese were also concurrently appointed.
translations.idiomatic: For all Han Banner posts Han Chinese were also appointed concurrently.

translations.literal: Its subordinates: one hall director, Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates included one Manchu hall director.

translations.literal: Directorate recorder □ directorate recorder — one Han.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate recorder (lacuna in source), one Han.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式，滿洲七人，漢軍三人。

translations.literal: Clerks — seven Manchu, three Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Manchu clerks and three Han Banner clerks.

sentences.zh: 又六所、一衛：曰左所，曰右所，曰中所，曰前所，曰後所，日馴象所，曰旗手衛。

translations.literal: Also six offices and one guard: namely the Left Office, the Right Office, the Central Office, the Front Office, the Rear Office, the Elephant-Training Office, and the Banner-Bearer Guard.
translations.idiomatic: It also had six offices and one guard: the Left Office, Right Office, Central Office, Front Office, Rear Office, Elephant-Training Office, and Banner-Bearer Guard.

translations.literal: Champion commissioners — originally regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Champion commissioners were originally regular third rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年改正四品，七年復故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi changed to regular fourth rank; in the seventh year restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 they were lowered to regular fourth rank; in year 7 restored.

sentences.zh: 宗室一人，滿洲、漢軍七人。

translations.literal: One from the imperial clan, seven Manchu and Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: One imperial clansman and seven Manchu and Han Banner posts.

translations.literal: Cloud-banner commissioners — originally regular fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-banner commissioners were originally regular fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年改正五品，七年復故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi changed to regular fifth rank; in the seventh year restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 they were lowered to regular fifth rank; in year 7 restored.

sentences.zh: 宗室二人，滿洲、漢軍十有八人。

translations.literal: Two from the imperial clan, eighteen Manchu and Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Two imperial clansmen and eighteen Manchu and Han Banner posts.

translations.literal: Directors of proper arrangement — originally regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of proper arrangement were originally regular fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年改正六品，七年復故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi changed to regular sixth rank; in the seventh year restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 they were lowered to regular sixth rank; in year 7 restored.

sentences.zh: 宗室三人，滿洲、漢軍二十有九人。

translations.literal: Three from the imperial clan, twenty-nine Manchu and Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Three imperial clansmen and twenty-nine Manchu and Han Banner posts.

translations.literal: Rectifiers of proper arrangement — originally regular sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Rectifiers of proper arrangement were originally regular sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年改從，七年復故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi changed to subordinate rank; in the seventh year restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 they were lowered to subordinate rank; in year 7 restored.

sentences.zh: 雍正十年升正五品，後復改從六品。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng raised to regular fifth rank; later again changed to subordinate sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 10 they were raised to regular fifth rank, then later reduced to subordinate sixth.

sentences.zh: 宗室三人，滿洲、漢軍二十有三人。

translations.literal: Three from the imperial clan, twenty-three Manchu and Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Three imperial clansmen and twenty-three Manchu and Han Banner posts.

sentences.zh: 鳴贊鞭官，由太常、鴻臚二寺贊禮郎、鳴贊官咨補。

translations.literal: Whip-acclamation officers were filled by consultation from ritual acclamation officers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Whip-acclamation officers were drawn from ritual acclamation officers of the Sacrifices and State Ceremonial courts.

translations.literal: Four Manchu, two in training.
translations.idiomatic: Four Manchu posts and two trainees.

sentences.zh: 鑾輿使掌供奉乘輿秩序鹵簿，辨其名物與其班列。

translations.literal: Imperial carriage commissioners managed the supply of imperial carriages, the order of regalia escorts, and distinguished their named objects and their formations.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial carriage commissioners managed imperial transport, regalia escort order, and the names, objects, and formations of each item.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀、朝會、時巡、大閱，帥所司供厥事。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, court assemblies, seasonal tours, and grand reviews, they led their offices to supply the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices, court assemblies, tours, and grand reviews they led their subordinates in providing these services.

translations.literal: The Left Office managed carriages, palanquins, and road equipment;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Office managed carriages, palanquins, and road equipment;

sentences.zh: 右所掌傘蓋、刀戟、弓矢、殳槍；

translations.literal: The Right Office managed umbrellas, canopies, blades, halberds, bows, arrows, shu spears, and lances;
translations.idiomatic: The Right Office umbrellas, canopies, blades, halberds, bows, arrows, shu spears, and lances;

sentences.zh: 中所掌麾氅、幡幢、纛幟、節鉞、仗馬；

translations.literal: The Central Office managed banners, pennants, streamers, great flags, batons of authority, and ceremonial horses;
translations.idiomatic: The Central Office banners, pennants, streamers, great flags, batons of authority, and ceremonial horses;

sentences.zh: 前所掌扇壚、瓶盂、杌椅、星拂、御仗、棕薦、靜鞭、品級山；

translations.literal: The Front Office managed fan screens, vases and bowls, stools and chairs, star-dusters, imperial staffs, palm mats, silence whips, and rank hills;
translations.idiomatic: The Front Office fan screens, ritual vessels, stools and chairs, star-dusters, imperial staffs, palm mats, silence whips, and rank hills;

translations.literal: The Rear Office managed banner claws and ceremonial staffs;
translations.idiomatic: The Rear Office banner claws and ceremonial staffs;

sentences.zh: 馴象所掌儀象、騎駕、鹵簿、前部大樂；

translations.literal: The Elephant-Training Office managed ritual elephants, mounted escort, regalia escorts, and front-section great music;
translations.idiomatic: The Elephant-Training Office ritual elephants, mounted escort, regalia escorts, and front-section great music;

sentences.zh: 旗手衛掌金鉦、鼓角、鐃歌大樂，兼午門司鐘，神武門鐘鼓樓直更。

translations.literal: The Banner-Bearer Guard managed golden gongs, drums and horns, and nao-song great music, and concurrently kept the Meridian Gate bells, and watch duty at the Divine Martial Gate bell-and-drum tower.
translations.idiomatic: The Banner-Bearer Guard handled golden gongs, drums, horns, and nao-song great music, kept the Meridian Gate bells, and stood watch at the Divine Martial Gate bell-and-drum tower.

translations.literal: Directors managed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Directors handled memorials.

translations.literal: Directorate recorders managed documents.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate recorders handled documents.

sentences.zh: 其別設者：往制，步輦雲麾使一人，治宜正三人，駕庫管理整宜尉二人，俱漢軍為之。

translations.literal: What was separately established: under the former system, for the palanquin one cloud-banner commissioner, three directors of proper arrangement, and two rectifiers managing the carriage store — all were Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Separate posts under the former system included one cloud-banner commissioner for the palanquin, three directors of proper arrangement, and two rectifiers for the carriage store—all Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 後分金、玉、象、革、木五輅，並拜褥、棕毯、蓖頭、亭座、駕衣諸管理，派冠軍使以次各官兼攝，則參用滿員。

translations.literal: Later the five chariots of gold, jade, elephant, leather, and wood were divided, along with managers of prayer mats, palm rugs, comb-heads, pavilion seats, and driving garments — champion commissioners and the various ranks below were assigned to hold these concurrently, and Manchus were also used.
translations.idiomatic: Later the five chariots—gold, jade, elephant, leather, and wood—and managers of prayer mats, palm rugs, comb-heads, pavilion seats, and driving garments were assigned to champion commissioners and lower ranks concurrently, with Manchus also participating.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，設錦衣衛，置指揮等官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the Brocade-Clad Guard was established, with commanders and other officers appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 the Brocade-Clad Guard was established with commanders and other officers.

sentences.zh: 明年，更名鑾儀衛，定各官品秩。

translations.literal: The next year it was renamed the Imperial Ceremonial Guard, and the ranks of its officers were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year it was renamed the Imperial Ceremonial Guard and officer ranks were fixed.

translations.literal: At the time there were five offices in all, but each office retained only one bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were five offices, each retaining only one bureau.

sentences.zh: 四年，省指揮使，置鑾儀使以次各官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the commander was abolished and ceremonial commissioners and the various ranks below were established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the commander post was abolished and imperial ceremonial commissioners and subordinate ranks were established.

sentences.zh: 明年，省副官及衛官百十有四人。

translations.literal: The next year, deputy officers and one hundred fourteen guard officers were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, deputy officers and 114 guard officers were cut.

sentences.zh: 六年，增攝政王下漢二品鑾儀使，三品冠軍使，四品雲麾使，五品治儀正，各二人；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, under the regent were added Han second-rank ceremonial commissioners, third-rank champion commissioners, fourth-rank cloud-banner commissioners, and fifth-rank directors of ceremony — two each;
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, under the regent, Han second-rank ceremonial commissioners, third-rank champion commissioners, fourth-rank cloud-banner commissioners, and fifth-rank directors of ceremony were added — two each;

translations.literal: Three rectifiers of ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: And three rectifiers of ceremony.

translations.literal: Later all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 九年，始以內大臣掌衛事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, grand ministers of the bodyguard first took charge of guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 grand ministers of the bodyguard first took charge of guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年置兼理衛事一人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong, one person was appointed to jointly manage guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 9 one post was added to jointly manage guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 十四年省，二十六年復置總理衛事內大臣一人，三十年又省。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year abolished; in the twenty-sixth year restored one grand minister of the bodyguard as overall manager of guard affairs; in the thirtieth year again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 14; in year 26 one bodyguard grand minister was restored as overall manager; abolished again in year 30.

sentences.zh: 十一年，定鑾儀使滿、漢各二人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, fixed at two Manchu and two Han ceremonial commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the quota was fixed at two Manchu and two Han ceremonial commissioners.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十一年省漢一人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Kangxi, one Han post was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31 one Han post was cut.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十年分滿使為左、右。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year of Qianlong, Manchu commissioners were divided into left and right.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 50 Manchu commissioners were split into left and right.

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year the former system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In year 57 the former system was restored.

translations.literal: Champion commissioners for accompanying sacrifices — two Han.
translations.idiomatic: Two Han champion commissioners for accompanying sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，掌步輦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, they managed palanquin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 they managed palanquin affairs.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，以一人掌庫事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, one person managed storehouse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 37 one person managed the storehouse.

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, all were discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In year 48 all were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 設左、右、中、前、後五所，鑾輿、馴馬、擎蓋、弓矢、旌節、幡幢、扇手、斧鉞、戈戟、班劍十司。

translations.literal: Established the Left, Right, Central, Front, and Rear five offices, with ten bureaus: imperial carriage, horse training, canopy bearing, bows and arrows, banners and batons, pennants and streamers, fan bearers, axes and yue, ge halberds and ji, and ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: The Left, Right, Central, Front, and Rear offices were established, with ten bureaus for carriages, horses, canopies, archery, insignia, banners, fans, axes, halberds, and ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 設馴像一所，分東、西二司。

translations.literal: Established one Elephant-Training Office, divided into eastern and western bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: One Elephant-Training Office was established, divided into eastern and western bureaus.

sentences.zh: 設旗手一衛，分左、右二司。

translations.literal: Established one Banner-Bearer Guard, divided into left and right bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: One Banner-Bearer Guard was established with left and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 定冠軍使十人，宗室一人，滿洲七人，漢軍二人。

translations.literal: Fixed ten champion commissioners — one from the imperial clan, seven Manchu, two Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ten champion commissioners were fixed: one clansman, seven Manchu, two Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 雲麾使二十有二人，宗室二人，滿洲十二人，漢軍八人。

translations.literal: Twenty-two cloud-banner commissioners — two from the imperial clan, twelve Manchu, eight Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two cloud-banner commissioners: two clansmen, twelve Manchu, eight Han Banner.

translations.literal: Six supernumeraries.
translations.idiomatic: Six supernumerary posts.

translations.literal: Manchu posts.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu posts.

sentences.zh: 治儀正二十有四人，宗室四人，漢軍二十人。

translations.literal: Twenty-four directors of ceremony — four from the imperial clan, twenty Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four directors of ceremony: four clansmen, twenty Han Banner.

translations.literal: Eighteen supernumeraries.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen supernumerary posts.

translations.literal: Manchu posts.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu posts.

sentences.zh: 整儀尉二十有九人，宗室四人，滿洲十有五人，漢軍十人。

translations.literal: Twenty-nine rectifiers of ceremony — four from the imperial clan, fifteen Manchu, ten Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine rectifiers of ceremony: four clansmen, fifteen Manchu, ten Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 十五年，省滿洲經歷一人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, one Manchu directorate recorder was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 one Manchu directorate recorder was cut.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，改經歷為漢缺，增置滿洲主事一人。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi, the directorate recorder became a Han post, and one Manchu director was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 the directorate recorder became a Han post and one Manchu director was added.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，增置鳴贊鞭官四人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, four whip-acclamation officers were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 four whip-acclamation officers were added.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年增學習二人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, two trainees were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 13 two trainees were added.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，置總辦、協辦、堂務、冠軍使各一人。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, one overall manager, one assistant manager, one hall affairs officer, and one champion commissioner were each established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 48 one each of overall manager, assistant manager, hall affairs officer, and champion commissioner was added.

translations.literal: Champion commissioners of the offices and guard served concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Office and guard champion commissioners served concurrently.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年更名綜理七所事務冠軍使，派雲麾使二人協理。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing, renamed champion commissioner for overall management of the seven offices' affairs, with two cloud-banner commissioners assigned to assist.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 6 the post was renamed champion commissioner for overall management of the seven offices, with two cloud-banner commissioners to assist.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十三年，省冠軍使二人，雲麾使八人，治儀正十人，整儀尉四人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu, two champion commissioners, eight cloud-banner commissioners, ten directors of ceremony, and four rectifiers of ceremony were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 33 two champion commissioners, eight cloud-banner commissioners, ten directors of ceremony, and four rectifiers were cut.

translations.literal: Imperial-clan quotas were fixed as listed above.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial-clan quotas were fixed as listed above.

translations.literal: The remainder were filled by Manchu and Han in combination.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining posts were shared between Manchu and Han appointees.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，避帝諱，改鑾儀使為鑾輿使，治儀正、整儀尉並易「儀」為「宜」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, to avoid the imperial taboo, ceremonial commissioners were renamed carriage commissioners, and directors and rectifiers of ceremony likewise changed "yi" to "yi".
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1, to avoid the imperial taboo, ceremonial commissioners became carriage commissioners and directors and rectifiers of ceremony changed "yi" to "yi" in their titles.

sentences.zh: 驍騎營八旗都統，初制正一品，後改從一品。

translations.literal: Vanguard Cavalry Brigade — commanders-in-chief of the Eight Banners: originally regular first rank, later changed to subordinate first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Cavalry Brigade commanders-in-chief of the Eight Banners: originally regular first rank, later subordinate first rank.

translations.literal: One each for Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: One each for Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner.

translations.literal: Deputy commanders-in-chief — regular second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commanders-in-chief — regular second rank.

translations.literal: Two from each banner.
translations.idiomatic: Two from each banner.

translations.literal: Regimental commanders — regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental commanders — regular third rank.

translations.literal: Deputy regimental commanders — regular fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy regimental commanders — regular fourth rank.

translations.literal: Ninety-six in all.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety-six in all.

sentences.zh: 滿洲、漢軍各四十人，蒙古十有六人。

translations.literal: Forty Manchu, forty Han Banner, and sixteen Mongol each.
translations.idiomatic: Forty Manchu, forty Han Banner, and sixteen Mongol each.

translations.literal: Company commanders — regular fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders — regular fourth rank.

translations.literal: Vanguard corporals — regular sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard corporals — regular sixth rank.

translations.literal: One thousand one hundred fifty-one in all.
translations.idiomatic: 1,151 in all.

sentences.zh: 滿洲各六百八十有一人，蒙古各二百有四人，漢軍各二百六十有六人。

translations.literal: Six hundred eighty-one Manchu, two hundred four Mongol, and two hundred sixty-six Han Banner each.
translations.idiomatic: 681 Manchu, 204 Mongol, and 266 Han Banner each.

translations.literal: Forty regimental commanders assisting in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Forty regimental commanders assisting in affairs.

sentences.zh: 滿洲、漢軍各十有六人，蒙古八人。

translations.literal: Sixteen Manchu, sixteen Han Banner, and eight Mongol each.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen Manchu, sixteen Han Banner, and eight Mongol each.

translations.literal: Selected from regimental commanders of their own banner.
translations.idiomatic: Selected from their own banner's regimental commanders.

sentences.zh: 章京，筆帖式，俱百四十有四人，滿洲各六十有四人，蒙古各三十有二人，漢軍各四十有八人。

translations.literal: Secretaries and clerks — one hundred forty-four in all: sixty-four Manchu, thirty-two Mongol, and forty-eight Han Banner each.
translations.idiomatic: 144 secretaries and clerks: 64 Manchu, 32 Mongol, and 48 Han Banner each.

sentences.zh: 隨印房行走散秩官無定員。

translations.literal: Ministers without portfolio serving in the seal office had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers without portfolio in the seal office had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 都統，副都統掌八旗政令，宣布敎養，釐詰戎兵，以贊旗務。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-chief and deputy commanders-in-chief managed the Eight Banners' government orders, proclaimed instruction and nurture, rectified soldiers, and assisted banner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-chief and deputies managed banner government orders, instruction, troop discipline, and banner affairs.

sentences.zh: 參領、副參領掌受事、付事以達佐領。

translations.literal: Regimental and deputy regimental commanders received and dispatched business to reach the company commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental and deputy regimental commanders routed business to company commanders.

sentences.zh: 佐領掌稽所治戶口田宅兵籍，歲時頒其敎戒。

translations.literal: Company commanders checked the households, fields, estates, and military registers under their charge, and yearly issued their admonitions and instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders audited households, property, and military registers and issued yearly instructions.

sentences.zh: 協理各官掌章奏文移，計會出納。

translations.literal: Coordinating officers managed memorials and documents and accounted for receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinating officers handled memorials, documents, and accounts.

translations.literal: The same for all camps.
translations.idiomatic: The same for all camps.

sentences.zh: 其特派者：直年旗大臣八人；

translations.literal: Those specially assigned: eight banner year-duty ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Special assignments included eight banner year-duty ministers;

sentences.zh: 其屬有參領，章京，筆帖式。

translations.literal: Their subordinates included regimental commanders, secretaries, and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: With regimental commanders, secretaries, and clerks under them.

translations.literal: Appointed from banner officials.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed from banner officials.

sentences.zh: 管理舊營房大臣，滿、蒙各一人；

translations.literal: Ministers managing old barracks — one Manchu and one Mongol each;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers managing old barracks — one Manchu and one Mongol each;

sentences.zh: 其屬有營總章京，驍騎校。

translations.literal: Their subordinates included barracks chief secretaries and vanguard corporals.
translations.idiomatic: With barracks chief secretaries and vanguard corporals under them.

sentences.zh: 新營房大臣，官房大臣，滿、蒙、漢軍各八人；

translations.literal: New barracks ministers and official-quarters ministers — eight each for Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner;
translations.idiomatic: New barracks and official-quarters ministers — eight each for Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner;

translations.literal: Their subordinates were the same as for old barracks.
translations.idiomatic: With the same subordinates as old barracks.

sentences.zh: 左、右翼鐵匠局副都統，其屬有參領，散秩官，驍騎校。

translations.literal: Left and right wing blacksmith-bureau deputy commanders-in-chief — their subordinates included regimental commanders, ministers without portfolio, and vanguard corporals.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right blacksmith-bureau deputy commanders-in-chief — with regimental commanders, ministers without portfolio, and vanguard corporals under them.

sentences.zh: 稽察寶坻等處駐防大臣，各二人；

translations.literal: Inspecting ministers for garrisons at Baodi and other places — two each;
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting ministers for Baodi and other garrisons — two each;

sentences.zh: 左、右翼世職官學總理大臣十人；

translations.literal: Overall managing ministers of the left and right hereditary-office schools — ten;
translations.idiomatic: Ten overall managing ministers for the left and right hereditary-office schools;

sentences.zh: 其屬有參領章京，清語、騎射敎習。

translations.literal: Their subordinates included regimental secretaries and Manchu-language and riding-and-archery instructors.
translations.idiomatic: With regimental secretaries and Manchu and riding-and-archery instructors.

sentences.zh: 十五善射處管理大臣，翼各一人；

translations.literal: Managing ministers of the Fifteen Skilled Archers Office — one for each wing;
translations.idiomatic: Managing ministers of the Fifteen Skilled Archers Office — one per wing;

sentences.zh: 漢軍清文義學稽察學務參領八人。

translations.literal: Eight Han Banner regimental commanders inspecting Manchu-script school affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Han Banner regimental commanders inspected Manchu-script school affairs.

sentences.zh: 其分攝者：俸饟處、馬册房、管理馬圈、籐牌營參領各官，漢軍鳥槍營領催各官，城門偏吉章京驍騎校，俱於旗員內選充。

translations.literal: Those with divided duties: salary-grain office, horse-register office, horse-pasture management, rattan-shield battalion regimental officers, Han Banner musket-battalion lead officers, and partial gate secretaries and vanguard corporals — all selected from banner officials.
translations.idiomatic: Divided duties included salary, horse registers, pastures, rattan-shield and musket battalions, and gate posts — all filled from banner officials.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖辛丑年，始編三百人爲一牛彔，置一額眞。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the Taizu's xinchou year, three hundred men were first organized as one niru, with one ejen appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in the Taizu's xinchou year, 300 men were organized as one niru with one ejen.

sentences.zh: 先是出兵校獵，人取一矢，一長領之，稱牛彔，至是遂以名官。

translations.literal: Earlier, on campaign and hunt, each man took one arrow and one leader commanded them, called a niru; now the name became an office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier on campaign and hunt each man carried one arrow under one leader, called a niru; the term now became an office.

sentences.zh: 天命元年編制滿洲牛彔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianming, Manchu niru were organized.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 1 Manchu niru were organized.

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Mongol niru were further organized.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Mongol niru were added.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong, Han Banner niru were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4 Han Banner niru were completed.

translations.literal: At first divided into four banners, soon increased to eight.
translations.idiomatic: They began as four banners and soon became eight.

sentences.zh: 乙卯年，定五牛彔置一扎蘭額眞，五扎蘭置一固山額眞，左、右梅勒額眞佐之。

translations.literal: In the yimao year, fixed that five niru placed one jalan ejen, five jalan one gushan ejen, with left and right meiren ejen assisting.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year, five niru formed one jalan with a jalan ejen; five jalan formed one gushan with a gushan ejen, assisted by left and right meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 太宗御極，置總管旗務八大臣，主政事；

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, eight great ministers overseeing banner affairs were established to preside over government;
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, eight great ministers overseeing banner affairs were established.

sentences.zh: 即固山額眞兼議政大臣。

translations.literal: That is, gushan ejen concurrently councillor ministers.
translations.idiomatic: These were gushan ejen who also served as councillor ministers.

sentences.zh: 佐管十六大臣，主理事聽訟。

translations.literal: Sixteen assisting managing ministers handled affairs and heard lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen assisting ministers handled affairs and lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 即梅勒額眞兼理事大臣。

translations.literal: That is, meiren ejen concurrently managing ministers.
translations.idiomatic: These were meiren ejen who also served as managing ministers.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，改額眞爲章京，固山額眞如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong, ejen was changed to zhangjing; gushan ejen remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 ejen became zhangjing; gushan ejen remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 管梅勒曰梅勒章京，管扎蘭曰扎蘭章京，管牛彔曰牛彔章京。

translations.literal: Those managing meiren were called meiren zhangjing, those managing jalan jalan zhangjing, those managing niru niru zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Meiren managers became meiren zhangjing, jalan managers jalan zhangjing, niru managers niru zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 其隨營馬兵曰阿禮哈超哈。

translations.literal: Camp cavalry were called alihahucha.
translations.idiomatic: Camp cavalry were called alihahucha.

sentences.zh: 是爲驍騎營之始，然猶統滿、蒙、漢軍爲一也。

translations.literal: This was the beginning of the Vanguard Cavalry Brigade, yet Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner were still under one command.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the start of the Vanguard Cavalry Brigade, though Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner were still unified.

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Mongol Eight Banners were first separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the Mongol Eight Banners were first established separately.

sentences.zh: 崇德七年，復分設漢軍八旗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongde, Han Banner Eight Banners were again separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 7 the Han Banner Eight Banners were established separately.

sentences.zh: 先是二年設二旗，四年分爲四。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the second year two banners were established; in the fourth year divided into four.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier two banners were set up in year 2 and split into four in year 4.

translations.literal: The system of twenty-four banners was then complete.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-four-banner system was then complete.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，定扎蘭章京漢字稱參領。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, jalan zhangjing was given the Chinese title regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 jalan zhangjing received the Chinese title regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 十七年，定固山額眞漢字稱都統，雍正元年改滿文固山額眞爲固山昂邦。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, gushan ejen was given the Chinese title commander-in-chief; in the first year of Yongzheng the Manchu gushan ejen was changed to gushan angbang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 gushan ejen became commander-in-chief; in Yongzheng 1 the Manchu term became gushan angbang.

sentences.zh: 梅勒章京稱副都統，牛彔章京稱佐領，分得撥什庫稱驍騎校，並定都統、副都統員額。

translations.literal: Meiren zhangjing was called deputy commander-in-chief, niru zhangjing company commander, fende bošokū vanguard corporal, and quotas for commanders-in-chief and deputies were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Meiren zhangjing became deputy commander-in-chief, niru zhangjing company commander, fende bošokū vanguard corporal, and commander quotas were fixed.

translations.literal: As listed above.
translations.idiomatic: As listed above.

sentences.zh: 參領，滿洲、漢軍旗各五人，蒙古各三人。

translations.literal: Regimental commanders: five each for Manchu and Han Banner, three each for Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental commanders: five each for Manchu and Han Banner, three for Mongol.

translations.literal: Soon one more was added to each.
translations.idiomatic: Soon one more was added to each.

translations.literal: Company commanders were fixed according to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Company-commander posts were set according to need.

sentences.zh: 分四等：部落長率屬歸誠，爰及苗裔，曰勳舊佐領；

translations.literal: Divided into four grades: a tribal chief leading his people in submission, extending to descendants — called meritorious hereditary company commander;
